judged_text: addGuestsHandler commits the new guests to Postgres via prisma.booking.update/attendees.createMany (lines 92-106) before the external calendar sync at line 165 runs, with no compensation for a calendar-side failure. A throw from eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (expired token, deleted external event, API error) leaves the guests already persisted in the DB, absent from the organizer's calendar, and the notification emails never sent because sendAddGuestsEmails is downstream; the mutation returns an error while the data was written, and every retry with the same emails is rejected because the dedupe filter at lines 74-78 now sees them as existing attendees and throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' — with no removeGuests mutation in the router, the DB/calendar divergence is permanent and only fixable by direct DB intervention.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees to Postgres first (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`, lines ~92-106), then performs the external calendar update (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, line ~165) with no transaction or compensation/rollback. Because `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch, any throw there will cause the mutation to error after the DB write has already succeeded, preventing the downstream `sendAddGuestsEmails` call and leaving DB/calendar out of sync. On a retry, `uniqueGuests` is recomputed from the (now updated) booking attendees and can become empty, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), making self-recovery impossible via this API (no removeGuests route shown in this diff).
